relationships.subject: Scn10a G1663S mutation
relationships.evidence_quote: Mutant mice were more sensitive to touch than wild types in the von Frey test.

relationships.subject: Scn10a G1663S mutation
relationships.evidence_quote: Therefore, Scn10aG1663S mutant mice showed a higher sensitivity to cool, but not cold temperatures.

relationships.subject: Scn10a G1663S mutation
relationships.evidence_quote: Therefore, Scn10aG1663S mutant male mice showed an increased sensitivity to heat.

relationships.subject: Scn10a G1663S mutation
relationships.evidence_quote: The Scn10aG1663S mutation did not alter the Scn10a transcript expression level in DRG in mutant mice of both sexes.

key_findings: Scn10a G1663S knock-in mice show increased mechanical, cool and (male) heat sensitivity without change in Scn10a expression or IENFD
Effects are sexually dimorphic: females more sensitive to cooling, males to radiant heat and 54C hot plate
